scope: Fort Chambly’s surviving stone fort at the Richelieu River as documented in June 2003. Includes four corner bastions, connecting masonry walls, the open inner courtyard and attached roofed ranges. The surrounding national historic site park, detached exhibits and interiors are outside the structure model.

originalReview.notes: Landward wall view shows masonry color, wall height relative to the bastion and the short upper bastion roof.

references.filename: Fort Chambly place d'armes and cannon.jpg

originalReview.notes: Courtyard view establishes the dressed openings, shingle roof, red dormer cheeks and lower arched bays.
River wall view shows rough stonework, near and far bastions, pale frames, wall bands and roof edge.

quallaSearch.notes: Three exact published Qualla originals by Petersent were accepted. The photographer identified these as self-photographed and explicitly dedicated each to the public domain. The hero photo with inferred authorship and the detail of a separate exhibit were excluded.
